author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through the existing visit form, under the same rules as booking. The correction changes that visit in place and returns to the owner's record; the pet gains no additional visit.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened (GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit), then the visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, model attribute 'visit') shows that visit's current date and description

given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted as its correction (POST to the same URL), then that visit carries them, the pet gains no additional visit, and the reader is redirected to the owner's record
given a blank description, when a correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again naming the description, and the stored visit is unchanged
given a date of today or earlier, when a correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again naming the date, and the stored visit is unchanged
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused, and no visit changes
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5 narrowed, NG-4 unchanged)
any link or other entry point to the correction from the owner's record or elsewhere: the owner decided the form is reachable by its URL alone in this request
a confirmation message after a correction: the request requires only the redirect
changing a visit's pet or owner
notes: PRD docs/prd.md (Visits, NG-5 row, Non-Goals preamble, Open Questions) and the non-goal ADRs were written in this dispatch. New ADR docs/adr/2026-10-01-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR status now points to it. docs/adr/README.md Index lacks the new row: it is outside this agent's write scope, and system-design-expert should add it. Narrowest-reading decisions, made without an owner answer and recorded as Open Questions in the PRD: (1) a past-dated visit cannot be corrected without moving its date past today, because the owner said the correction validates like creation; (2) no confirmation message; (3) edge case 3, refusing a visitId outside the named pet, is the product expert's reading of 'updates that visit'; the presentation of the refusal follows the existing behavior for an unknown pet. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction follows the existing edit-in-place pattern in the owner package. PetController's @ModelAttribute("pet") loader (findPet, optional petId path variable: new entity when absent, existing one when present) already demonstrates it; found by grep of PetController.java, which is the weaker basis because the IDE oracle is not connected. The adjustment: VisitController's loadPetWithVisit resolves the existing Visit through Pet when a visitId path variable is present. It attaches a new Visit only when visitId is absent (the booking routes). Pet gains a lookup of one of its visits by identity. The correction is saved through OwnerRepository by cascade, per the system-design.md Contracts invariant (Owner is the aggregate entry point; no VisitRepository). No new module, type, or pattern. system-design.md was updated for REQ-VIS-003: the Contracts rows (Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController), the invariant line, the Threat Model mass-assignment row, a new Known Defects row, and a new § Scale and Load section with this slice's row.
integration_points: Entry points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit in VisitController. Both render pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with model attribute 'visit'; a successful POST redirects to /owners/{ownerId}. The form has no action attribute, so it posts back to the edit URL unchanged.

Binding target for the POST /visits/{visitId}/edit entry point: the persisted Visit behind an allow-list of 'date' and 'description', via a visit-scoped @InitBinder("visit") in VisitController. The controller-wide id/*.id disallow stays (security-principles.md § Realization, Mass assignment row). The allow-list also applies to booking's 'visit'; that path only offers date and description, so booking behaviour is unchanged. The edit handler must not bind the Owner: take it as @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) or read it from the model, never as a bound @ModelAttribute Owner.

Repository boundary double: the existing class-level @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub in VisitControllerTests (a framework stub). Neither alternative fits: OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, so a hand-written double would have to implement the whole inherited surface, and the test class is a @WebMvcTest slice with no datasource for the real repository (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: existing stubs are tolerated). Assert 'no additional visit' and 'visit carries the new values' on the Owner passed to save (captor or verify-argument). Assert 'stored visit unchanged' as save never being called.
Framework transport double: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).
Unknown or foreign visitId (edge case 3): the loader throws IllegalArgumentException, matching the existing unknown-owner and unknown-pet behaviour in the same loader. No save happens.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader with an optional path variable: a new entity when absent, the existing aggregate member when present
edit handler shape: validate, re-render on errors, save the owner, redirect to /owners/{ownerId}
the non-future visit-date rule; correction must share it, extracted once rather than duplicated

risks.risk: Phantom visit: the class-wide @ModelAttribute("visit") loader currently runs for every handler and attaches a new Visit to the pet. If it runs on the edit routes, saving the owner cascades an extra visit. That breaks 'the pet gains no additional visit' (system-design.md Contracts invariant: visits are persisted only by cascade from Owner).
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on the optional visitId path variable, as PetController.findPet does. Assert in the success test that the saved pet's visit count is unchanged.

risks.risk: The future-date rule gets duplicated between booking and correction. It is a business rule living in a controller, the existing gap against architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog, Web controller row (system-design.md Open Question 2).
risks.mitigation: Keep the rule in one private method of VisitController that both handlers call. Moving it into the domain is outside this slice; the open question stays open.

risks.risk: Mass assignment on the new POST: binding the owner, or Visit fields beyond the form (security-principles.md § Realization, Mass assignment row).
risks.mitigation: Allow-list date and description on the 'visit' binder, keep the id disallow, and don't bind the Owner on the edit handler (system-design.md Threat Model, mass-assignment row).

risks.risk: Looking up a visit by identity scales with the pet's visit count (system-design.md § Scale and Load, the 'A pet's visits, resolved by visit identity' row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear scan over the eagerly loaded visit set, per the row. No query or index.

risks.risk: The reused template says 'New' and 'Add Visit' unconditionally on the submit button. A user-facing text change must exist in every message bundle (REQ-LANG-002, enforced by the bundle-parity test).
risks.mitigation: The request mandates neither a heading nor a button change, so leaving the template untouched is the narrowest reading. The 'New' heading is already conditional on visit['new']. If the button text is varied, reuse an existing key or add the new key to all eleven bundles.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records, so it was skipped. The ADR index row for docs/adr/2026-10-01-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md was added to docs/adr/README.md, as the prd-entry notes asked. The 2026-08-08 row's index status now mirrors that ADR's narrowed status. No new ADR: the design reuses the PetController pattern and constrains no later slice. New durable observation: visit booking binds request fields onto the loaded Owner (processNewVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner) and saves it. It is recorded in system-design.md Known Defects as derived and unconfirmed, and this slice does not fix it. Open questions, recorded and not waited on, since the owner said no further product answers will come. (1) Concurrent corrections of the same visit are last-write-wins: no entity carries a version column, the same as owner and pet edit. (2) On a refused correction, the previous-visits table on the redisplayed form shows the edited visit with the rejected values. Those values are in memory only and never stored, so the 'stored visit unchanged' criterion still holds. (3) Edge case 3's refusal presentation is the error page, matching the existing unknown-pet behaviour; whether it should be a not-found response is not decided.

findings.description: Pet.getVisit is a domain rule the design doc assigns to Pet (system-design.md:90 'resolves one of them by identity'), i.e. below the web boundary, and it has three paths (skip unsaved visit, match by id, null). The one scoping test, theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitNotBelongingToThePet, posts id 99, which exists on no pet. approved_aspects: Ownership scoping holds on the new edit routes. The visit is found through the owner, then the pet, then the visit (VisitController.java:73 `Owner owner = optionalOwner.orElseThrow(`, :76 `Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);`, :84 `Visit existingVisit = pet.getVisit(visitId);`), and a visit id that does not belong to the pet throws before any binding or save. Mass assignment is closed on the correction path. The new `@InitBinder("visit")` adds `setAllowedFields("date", "description")` (VisitController.java:58) and the global `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (:53) still applies. The edit handler takes the owner as `@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, so request params cannot overwrite owner fields before `owners.save(owner)`. The allow-list also narrows the existing booking route's Visit binding, which strengthens it. The pre-existing booking-route owner binding is recorded in system-design.md Known Defects and is not extended by this change

The correction path persists only validated data. `@Valid Visit` enforces `@NotBlank` on the description, and the future-date rule is now one shared helper, rejectDateNotInFuture, used by both booking and correction, so no path skips it. No injection or escaping sink was added. The Java diff adds no query text, shell call, file I/O, Jackson type config, or /tmp use. blast_radius.note: Contained to the owner package: 57 prod lines across Pet.getVisit and VisitController's new GET/POST edit route, with the rest tests and docs. semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the request says. The visit is resolved only among this pet's saved visits, and an unknown id throws before binding or save. The owner is bound with binding=false, the same future-date rule is extracted and shared, and on failure nothing is saved. The new @InitBinder("visit") allow-list also applies to booking, but Visit only has date, description and an already-disallowed id, so booking behavior does not change. Two user-visible consequences are documented, not hidden: a visit whose date has passed cannot be corrected at all (PRD open question), and the reused template still shows an 'Add Visit' button on the correction form.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes. Updating in place checks the same instance and that the pet has a single visit. Blank-description and non-future-date refusals verify save is never called. Owner and id tampering are pinned. PetTests covers resolving another pet's visit and an unsaved visit, so dropping the isNew guard or widening the lookup would fail a test. The residual is that persistence runs against a mocked OwnerRepository, so the JPA merge of the corrected visit is not exercised. That matches the existing suite's pattern.
